name: Utilities
title: Water network incident coordination
summary: Assemble pressure, asset, and customer-impact evidence for operator-owned water-network response.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A water utility receives low-pressure alarms and customer reports across several neighborhoods. Operators need to reconcile telemetry, planned works, pipe topology, and field observations before dispatching crews or changing network configuration. Agents prepare situational evidence without operating pumps, valves, or public-health decisions.
problem: Customer reports may be duplicated or geocoded incorrectly, while telemetry can fail during the same incident. Inferring a pipe break from a pressure pattern alone can misdirect crews. Network topology and isolation boundaries require engineering validation.
whyAgents: Telemetry, asset-graph, field-work, and customer-impact specialists investigate different evidence channels. The workflow keeps confirmed observations separate from modeled exposure and routes consequential decisions to established utility roles.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Assess evidence quality and coordination time alongside field response. Service restoration and public-health outcomes require accountable operational decisions; the agent contribution is an inspectable, current picture of what is known and what still needs verification.

agents.name: Telemetry investigator
agents.responsibility: Compare pressure and flow observations with sensor health and planned operating changes.
agents.boundary: Cannot set pump targets or change alarm thresholds.

agents.name: Asset dependency agent
agents.responsibility: Trace candidate pipe segments and connected service areas using governed network data.
agents.boundary: Cannot authorize isolation boundaries or assume map accuracy.

agents.name: Field coordination agent
agents.responsibility: Locate active work orders, crew availability, and verified field reports.
agents.boundary: Cannot dispatch unsafe work or bypass site access procedures.

agents.name: Customer impact agent
agents.responsibility: Group reports and draft factual service updates from approved incident status.
agents.boundary: Cannot issue health guidance or publish notices without authorized review.

systems.name: Operational telemetry gateway
systems.role: Exports observations without providing a write path to control equipment.

systems.name: Geographic and asset management systems
systems.role: Provide pipe topology, valves, maintenance history, and map revision metadata.

systems.name: Incident and customer platforms
systems.role: Own crew assignments, approved public statements, and report follow-up responsibilities.

flow.title: Correlate incoming reports
flow.description: Deduplicate customer cases and alarms by location and time while retaining individual evidence and uncertain addresses.

flow.title: Check telemetry reliability
flow.description: Compare sensor health, neighboring observations, and recent operational changes before accepting a pressure pattern.

flow.title: Map possible exposure
flow.description: Trace affected segments using current asset data and label modeled impact separately from confirmed service disruption.

flow.title: Gather field context
flow.description: Retrieve active works and verified crew observations; surface conflicts between map records and physical findings.

flow.title: Prepare operator options
flow.description: Show inspection priorities, uncertain isolation assumptions, and a draft customer update for the appropriate operational owner.

flow.title: Track authorized response
flow.description: Record approved dispatch and communication receipts, then reconcile field findings and telemetry before closing the incident.

diagrams.caption: A pressure sensor fails during the incident. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A pressure sensor fails during the incident.
failures.detection: Sensor diagnostics and neighboring measurements disagree with the isolated reading.
failures.recovery: Exclude the suspect signal from confirmed evidence and request field validation without suppressing the incident.

failures.scenario: A field crew discovers a valve absent from the map.
failures.detection: Verified field report conflicts with the asset revision used in the plan.
failures.recovery: Suspend map-dependent recommendations and route topology correction to engineering before further isolation planning.

controls: Prevent agent access to pump, valve, and supervisory-control write interfaces.
Require operational approval for dispatch and separate authorized review for public-health messages.
Label confirmed outages, customer reports, and modeled exposure as distinct evidence classes.
Protect customer addresses in aggregated incident views and telemetry exports.
Attach asset-map revision and field verification status to every network-dependent proposal.

metrics.name: Situational packet latency
metrics.definition: Time from incident registration to operator-reviewable evidence and proposed next checks.

metrics.name: Location resolution quality
metrics.definition: Audited reports assigned to the correct service area divided by audited geocoded reports.

metrics.name: Field contradiction rate
metrics.definition: Plans requiring revision after verified field findings divided by plans reviewed in the field.

metrics.name: Communication consistency
metrics.definition: Published updates matching approved incident state divided by sampled published updates.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces reliance on any single failed sensor.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires careful uncertainty labels and location reconciliation.
Agents cannot directly shorten physical response execution.
Outdated topology can create misleading impact estimates.

rollout.acceptance: Operators validate location matching, sensor failures, and map contradictions against completed incidents.
One service district reviews evidence packets and checks customer-data minimization.
Dispatch drafts and notices enter existing workflows after stale-map and contradictory-field-report drills succeed.
